scene_translation: The bartender, polishing a glass, quietly set a single photograph on the counter. "This is something your grandmother left behind. It was thirty years ago now, but she said someday you would come." In the photograph stood a young woman before the torii gate of an unfamiliar shrine, and beside her was the figure of another woman dressed in a blue one-piece. "The one in blue — she should still be somewhere in this city."
grammar_note: 【はずだ】 expresses the speaker's confident expectation based on reasoning: 「いるはずだ」 = "she should be / must be there." Note also the bartender's speech register — formal but not stiff, using 「〜だ」 over 「〜です」, and the respectful 「お祖母さん」 and 「〜の方」. This measured, slightly archaic masculine register contrasts with how a younger character might speak.

mystery_memo: The photograph is the central artifact — it confirms the woman in blue is real, connected to the player's grandmother, and still alive in Tokyo. The bartender is now firmly allied (friendly) — he has waited thirty years to deliver this item and speaks with quiet gravity. The shrine in the photo is unidentified; it will become a key location around scene 7-8. The woman in blue has now been glimpsed in the photo before appearing in person — her first true appearance should come in scene 5 or 6, triggered by whichever path the player takes. The grandmother's connection to both the bar and the woman in blue is the core of the mystery: they knew something about this neighborhood that was meant to be passed on.
